input.query:
MATCH (i:Indicator)-[:ABOUT]->(a:Account)
OPTIONAL MATCH (i)-[:CONTRIBUTING]->(c:Transfer)
OPTIONAL MATCH p = (c)-[:PASSED_ON*1..15]->(t:Transfer)
WITH i, a, collect(p) AS ps
WITH i, a, [p IN ps | [n IN tail(nodes(p)) | n]] AS lists
UNWIND (CASE WHEN size(lists)=0 THEN [[]] ELSE lists END) AS l
UNWIND (CASE WHEN size(l)=0 THEN [null] ELSE l END) AS ot
OPTIONAL MATCH (ot)-[:TO]->(r:Account)
WITH i, a, collect(DISTINCT r.id) AS rs
RETURN i.id, a.id, rs AS onward_receivers ORDER BY i.id

findings.statement: Scope: one bounded replay (run:5ce89f521e5e), with 50,000 dataset events, 3 of 3 jobs completed, clink exit status 0, not cancelled. Parameters: at least 5 distinct senders per event-time hour, onward gap at most 1,800,000 ms. The graph holds 50,000 transfers, 12,072 accounts, 12,321 devices, 691 onward links and 6 fan-in alerts. Everything below holds only for this dataset as this run processed it.

Alert A-10859 (window 1794924000000–1794927600000): 6 senders, 6 transfers, total 204,000. Every contributing transfer starts a candidate onward-transfer path. The paths branch through A-78340 (T011583, T011670). Up to 3 onward links lead to two end accounts: A-92332 (via T011600 to A-75793, then T011628) and A-85287 (via T011695). Path accounts: A-10859, A-78340, A-75793, A-92332, A-85287.

Alert A-37573 (window 1794823200000–1794826800000): 7 senders, 7 transfers, total 379,500, the largest of the six. All 7 contributing transfers start paths, and every path has exactly 4 onward links. The paths follow the same account sequence twice at different times: A-37573 → A-38045 → A-93288 → A-63022 → A-54215, first via T003168/T003182/T003201/T003222, then via T003391/T003416/T003433/T003454. All paths end at A-54215.

Alert A-83577 (window 1795057200000–1795060800000): 8 senders, 8 transfers, total 174,500. All 8 contributing transfers lead into one linear sequence of 5 onward links (T022572, T022592, T022609, T022629, T022649) through A-56768, A-83094, A-43725 and A-14799. It ends at A-39382. This is the deepest reach of the six alerts.

Alert A-20636 (window 1795190400000–1795194000000): 6 senders, 6 transfers, total 36,000. Five contributing transfers lead by one onward link (T033506, 30,000) to A-36729, where the paths end. T033316 has no onward link.

Alert A-85921 (window 1794855600000–1794859200000): 6 senders, 6 transfers, total 15,000. Every contributing transfer is exactly 2,500, for example T005750 and T005978. Four contributing transfers lead by one onward link (T005888, 9,500) to A-10758, where the paths end. T005934 and T005978 have no onward link.

Alert A-28137 (window 1795003200000–1795006800000): 7 senders, 7 transfers, total 29,500. None of its 7 contributing transfers has an onward link, so it has no candidate onward-transfer paths. A-28137's only recorded outgoing transfer is T018852 (21,000 to A-87539 at 1795013700000). That is 7,440,000 ms after its last contributing credit (T018248), outside the 30-minute onward window, and T018852 has no onward link itself.

Shared devices on routes: (a) A-37573: device D-45880 sent all 8 of its onward transfers, from four path accounts (A-37573, A-38045, A-93288, A-63022). (b) A-10859: device D-79802 was used by A-10859 and A-78340. (c) A-83577: device D-40018 was used by the non-adjacent path accounts A-83094 and A-14799. The same device was also used, much later, by off-route account A-34114 for T038409, which has no onward link. Every other path account sent from a separate device.
No device was used to send by two or more path accounts for alerts A-20636, A-85921 and A-28137.
None of the end accounts (A-92332, A-85287, A-54215, A-39382, A-36729, A-10758) has a fan-in alert of its own.

The six alerts look alike as indicators (6–8 distinct senders, one transfer per sender, inside one hour). The recorded relationships separate them into three groups. (1) A-37573, A-83577 and A-10859: every contributing transfer has an onward link, the paths reach 3–5 links deep, and onward amounts are close to the window total. In these three, path accounts share a device: one device across four accounts for A-37573, two accounts for A-10859, two non-adjacent accounts plus one off-route account for A-83577. (2) A-20636 and A-85921: one onward link to a single account, not all contributions linked, and no shared device. (3) A-28137: no onward links and no shared device. Interpretation follows the timing and device records only. For group 3 the only recorded relationship is the fan-in itself. Groups 1 and 2 also have recorded timing links, and group 1 adds device overlap.

hypotheses.statement: A-37573's sequence may be a single-operator layering route. One device sent every onward transfer from four accounts, the same account sequence happened twice, and each step was slightly smaller than the one before. A shared device does not establish common control or identity, and onward links record timing only, not that the same funds moved.
A-10859 and A-78340 may be controlled by the same party, given shared device D-79802. A-83094 and A-14799 may be related through D-40018. This could equally reflect a shared or public device.

A-28137 may be an ordinary collection account, for example many small payments to one payee. A-85921's uniform 2,500 contributions may reflect a fixed-price payment or a scripted pattern. The data does not distinguish these possibilities.

unresolved.question: What happens at end accounts A-92332, A-85287, A-54215, A-39382, A-36729 and A-10758 beyond this dataset? A path ending here means only that no further qualifying transfer exists in this bounded replay.
Who owns or uses devices D-45880, D-79802 and D-40018, and how is A-34114 related to A-83094 and A-14799, if at all? The data records only device use per transfer.
Do the onward transfers carry the same funds as the contributing credits? Onward links record timing only, and no balance or fund-tracing data is available.
Is anything known about the contributing senders (customer data, earlier history outside this replay)? None of them shares a device with any other account in this dataset.
